author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacts to Jon Stewart’s comments about newly surfaced air-quality records from the aftermath of 9/11 and the claim that New York officials knew Ground Zero air was dangerous long before the public was properly informed. From there, he questions who gets to define “misinformation,” why major crises so often seem to benefit powerful institutions, and how the public is supposed to know whom to trust.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell revisits the collapse of World Trade Center 7 on September 11, questioning how a 47-storey building that was not struck by a plane came down later that day. He contrasts the official explanation of fire and structural damage with the way the collapse appeared, before broadening the discussion into distrust of government, the Patriot Act and the wars that followed 9/11.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell breaks down a controversial surveillance program originally exposed by Edward Snowden, one that keeps getting reauthorized under a rotating cast of justifications, terrorism first, now tracking cartels and their supply chains. He calls out the irony directly, a system quick to condemn certain rhetoric elsewhere is apparently fine using it themselves if it helps force through legislation that keeps ordinary people under surveillance. With the original justification no longer holding up, he argues this is simply the next excuse being manufactured to justify the same overreach. A sharp breakdown of how the excuse changes but the surveillance never does.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacts to the UK announcing the largest ever national pandemic exercise, complete with new powers attached, and can't help but point out how convenient the timing sounds. He's careful not to attack the politician making the announcement personally, acknowledging he's probably a decent, well meaning person, but argues he's been captured by a system that ultimately serves state interests over public ones.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell opens up about his genuine friendship with Jonathan Roumie, the actor who plays Jesus in The Chosen, tracing it back to meeting him years earlier on the set of the HBO show Ballers, where Roumie worked as his body double. Russell admits he stood out from a lot of the actors he crossed paths with because he actually liked spending time with him, staying friends long after they stopped working together, right up through Roumie telling him about the small crowdfunded scripture project that eventually became The Chosen. A warm, genuine story about an unexpected friendship.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Candace Owens gets emotional describing what she calls the hardest part of losing her friend Charlie Kirk, wondering whether the life he lived was ever fully real, comparing it to The Truman Show. She describes feeling isolated for simply asking questions in the aftermath, treated as an outsider rather than someone fighting for answers about what happened to him. A raw, emotional moment from someone still processing a personal loss in the public eye.
